## Hands-on 2 – The data, the estimand and the graph {#hands-on-2-the-data-the-estimand-and-the-graph .smaller}

::: {.small}
**Task 2** has three pieces:

1. **Look at the data.** Count the unions of each survey and the `r fmt_n(sum(paper_unions$cycle == "1995"))` and `r fmt_n(sum(paper_unions$cycle == "2006-10"))` unions of the paper with their outcomes; compute the weighted shares of the women who cohabit in each cohort; turn the unions into person-months with `spec_frame(unions)`, and draw the life table
2. **Write the estimand statement.** Fill every bracket of the template for *this* claim, above all which cohorts and what is held constant
3. **Finish the graph.** Take the `#` off `"period -> marriage"` if you believe it, then run `adjustmentSets(dag)`, `paths(dag, Z = "cohabits")` and `paths(dag, Z = c("cohabits", "education", "race"))`; then add `"period -> age_start"`
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Two sentences for your notes: **what does keeping only cohabitors do to the comparison of the two periods, and which adjustment set answers which reading of "cohabitors"?**
:::

::: {.fragment .small}
Whatever you decide here is your starting point on the menu in Task 4, and field 4 of the preregistration in Task 5.
:::

::: notes

Then turn the unions into person-months with the helper and draw the life table; the code is in your report.
